title: AI for Business Intelligence: Transform Data with ai for business intelligence
summary: Leverage AI for business intelligence to turn ecommerce data into actionable insights with predictive analytics and smarter decisions.
body_text: AI for Business Intelligence: Transform Data with ai for business intelligence Mariam Ahmed Co-founder & CTO · January 23, 2026 Imagine your business intelligence could tell you what’s coming, not just what already happened. This is the core shift that AI for business intelligence delivers. It turns your data from a rearview mirror into a forward-looking guide, helping your whole team make smarter calls. Moving from Reactive Dashboards to Proactive Decisions Traditional business intelligence (BI) is all about dashboards. These static reports are great for showing you historical data—last month’s sales, website traffic, you name it—but they put all the work on you. You have to connect the dots, find the trends, and figure out why the numbers moved. It’s a completely reactive process. AI flips this model on its head. Instead of just showing you data, an AI-driven system acts like a proactive analyst. Think of it like a satnav that doesn’t just show your current spot but warns you about a traffic jam up ahead and suggests a better route before you get stuck. For modern e-commerce brands, this is a fundamental change. The Shift to Forward-Looking Insights The conversation completely changes. You stop asking, “What were last week’s sales?” and start getting automated alerts like, “Your conversion rate from TikTok ads is projected to drop 20% this week due to ad fatigue.” That isn’t just data; it’s a decision-ready insight that lets you act immediately. This proactive power comes from AI’s ability to analyse huge datasets from multiple sources at once—think Shopify, Google Ads, and Meta. It finds the subtle patterns and connections that are almost impossible for a human to spot in a spreadsheet. An AI-powered BI system doesn’t just report the news; it writes the headlines for what’s coming next, giving your team a critical head start. Turning Data into Your Strategic Asset This evolution from reactive reports to proactive analysis fundamentally changes how you run your business. Instead of spending hours digging through dashboards to figure out a problem, your team gets alerts that pinpoint the issue and often suggest a solution. This frees up precious time for strategy and execution. Key benefits of going proactive include: Early Issue Detection: Spot problems like a drop in customer lifetime value or rising acquisition costs before they seriously damage your bottom line. Opportunity Identification: Uncover hidden growth drivers, like a high-performing customer segment you weren’t even targeting. Improved Forecasting: Get more accurate predictions for inventory, sales, and resource planning. To move beyond reactive dashboards and achieve truly proactive decisions, leveraging AI demand forecasting is essential for optimising inventory and boosting growth. How AI Unlocks Deeper Data Insights To get your head around how AI changes business intelligence, think of your data as a massive library. Traditional BI is like giving you the library card and the catalogue. You know which books exist and where to find them, but you still have to do all the reading yourself. AI, on the hand, is like having a team of expert librarians who have already read every single book. They understand the connections between them, and when you have a question, they don’t just point you to a shelf—they hand you the exact paragraph you need. This isn’t magic; it’s just a stack of powerful technologies working in concert. When we break down the core components— Natural Language Processing , Machine Learning , and Predictive Analytics —we can see exactly how AI elevates your data from a simple record into a genuine decision-making engine for your brand. Speaking the Language of Your Data with NLP The first big shift comes from Natural Language Processing (NLP) . This is the tech that lets you talk to your data just by asking questions in plain English, the same way you’d ask a colleague for a number. Instead of wrestling with filters in a spreadsheet or configuring a dashboard, you can just ask, “Which customer segment has the highest lifetime value?” or “What was our return on ad spend for our latest Meta campaign?” NLP translates your plain-language question into a query the machine understands, crunches the relevant data, and serves up a clear answer. For busy e-commerce operators, this completely removes the technical barrier that usually stands between a business question and a data-backed insight. Uncovering Hidden Patterns with Machine Learning Next up, Machine Learning (ML) algorithms act as your tireless data detectives. These systems are built to continuously sift through enormous datasets from all your connected platforms—your Shopify store, Google Ads , and Klaviyo account—to spot patterns a human analyst would almost certainly miss. To really appreciate how AI unlocks these deeper insights, it’s crucial to understand how to analyze marketing data for data-driven decisions . For instance, an ML model might identify a specific sequence of behaviours that signals a customer is about to churn. It could spot a customer who has slowed their purchase frequency, stopped opening marketing emails, and recently visited your returns page. By flagging this customer before they leave, you get a shot at proactively re-engaging them with a targeted offer. Machine learning finds the “why” behind the “what.” It moves beyond just reporting that sales are down and actually identifies the root cause, like a specific ad campaign underperforming with a key demographic. This is what makes AI for business intelligence so powerful. It connects the dots across your entire operation, revealing relationships between marketing spend, customer behaviour, and sales that you never would have known existed. A Quick Comparison The shift from manual reporting to proactive analysis is a fundamental one. Here’s a quick breakdown of what that actually means for an e-commerce operator. Traditional BI vs AI-Powered BI A Quick Comparison Capability Traditional BI (Dashboards & Reports) AI-Powered BI (Proactive Analysis) How it Works You pull data and build reports to find answers. The system finds insights and brings them to you. Pace of Analysis Weekly or monthly reporting cycles. Backward-looking. Continuous, real-time monitoring. Forward-looking. Skill Requirement Needs someone skilled in Excel, SQL, or BI tools. Anyone can ask questions in plain English. Key Output Static dashboards showing “what happened”. Actionable alerts explaining “why it happened”. Typical Question “What were our sales last week?” “Why did our repeat purchase rate drop yesterday?” Strategic Value Good for historical performance tracking. Drives proactive, day-to-day decision-making. The old way gives you a rear-view mirror. The new way gives you a GPS that also points out traffic jams ahead. Forecasting the Future with Predictive Analytics Finally, predictive analytics takes all your historical data and uses it to forecast what’s likely to happen next. It builds on the patterns uncovered by machine learning to create sophisticated models that project future outcomes with a surprising degree of accuracy. Think of it as your business’s own private weather forecast. Instead of just guessing, you get data-backed projections you can actually plan around. Inventory Management: Predict which products will sell out next month based on sales velocity, seasonality, and your marketing calendar, so you can reorder stock just in time. Sales Projections: Forecast quarterly revenue based on current conversion rates and projected website traffic from your upcoming campaigns. Customer Behaviour: Identify which new customers are most likely to become repeat purchasers, letting you focus your retention efforts where they’ll have the biggest impact. By combining NLP, ML, and predictive analytics, AI gives your team the clear, forward-looking answers needed to drive sustainable growth. It stops your data from being a dusty historical record and turns it into an active, strategic asset. Practical AI Use Cases for E-Commerce Brands Understanding the theory behind AI is one thing, but seeing it sell more products is what really matters. For e-commerce and direct-to-consumer brands, AI for business intelligence isn’t an abstract concept—it’s a practical tool that impacts everything from marketing budgets to stock levels. It’s about replacing guesswork with data-backed confidence. Instead of hunting through disconnected dashboards, your teams get clear, automated insights that tell them what to do next. This means you can solve problems before they start hurting your bottom line and jump on opportunities faster than your competitors. Let’s look at a few real-world examples. Optimising Marketing Spend with Automated Insights Marketing teams are constantly juggling budgets across platforms like Meta and Google, trying to nail the perfect allocation. An AI analyst automates this entire discovery process, providing continuous monitoring and actionable advice that a human simply couldn’t produce at the same scale or speed. Imagine an AI system plugged into your ad accounts and your Shopify store. It doesn’t just report on Return on Ad Spend (ROAS); it actively looks for trouble. For instance, the system might notice that a specific Facebook ad creative—a top performer for three weeks straight—is now showing signs of ad fatigue . Its click-through rate is dipping while its cost-per-acquisition is slowly creeping up. Instead of you spotting this in a weekly report, the AI sends an immediate alert: “Heads up: Your ‘Summer Campaign - Video Ad 3’ is showing a 15% drop in efficiency. We recommend reallocating £500 of its daily budget to the ‘New Arrivals - Carousel Ad,’ which has a 22% higher conversion rate this week.” This isn’t just data; it’s a direct, revenue-protecting instruction. Your marketing team can act decisively, shifting budget to winning campaigns and cutting losses on underperformers before they waste serious money. The shift towards this kind of intelligent automation is accelerating. In the UK, AI adoption among businesses has skyrocketed, with more than half ( 52% ) now using AI technologies—a massive jump from just 39% the previous year. Among those adopters, a whopping 92% report increased revenue . This proves that tools connecting to Shopify, Google Analytics, and Meta Ads can deliver the decision-ready insights needed to spot performance dips, customer trends, or marketing wins in real time. You can learn more from the full AWS report on AI adoption . Preventing Stockouts with Predictive Inventory Management For an operations manager, few things are more painful than a stockout on a bestselling product. It means lost sales, unhappy customers, and a potential hit to your search rankings. Traditional inventory management often relies on historical sales data and manual forecasts, which can easily miss a sudden spike in demand. An AI analyst changes the game by applying predictive models. By monitoring real-time sales velocity from Shopify, analysing website traffic from Google Analytics, and even factoring in your marketing calendar, the system can forecast demand with far greater accuracy. Here’s how that plays out: Early Warnings: The AI detects a particular product is being added to carts at a rate 30% higher than the weekly average. Contextual Analysis: It checks this against your marketing data and sees you just launched a new influencer campaign featuring that exact item. Proactive Alert: You get a notification weeks in advance: “Based on current sales velocity and campaign performance, you are projected to sell out of ‘Product X’ in 18 days. We recommend placing a new purchase order now to avoid a stockout.” This kind of proactive alert system turns your operations team from reactive problem-solvers into strategic planners. For a deeper look at how this works, check out our guide on how to analyse Shopify data to boost e-commerce growth . Uncovering Hidden Costs and True Profitability Finance leaders in e-commerce often struggle to get a clear picture of true profitability. Manually mashing up Shopify sales data with advertising costs, shipping fees, and transaction charges in spreadsheets is tedious and full of errors. An AI-powered BI tool automates this entire financial analysis. By pulling in all your financial data streams, the AI can calculate the precise contribution margin for a specific product line or even a single SKU. It can uncover hidden costs you might be missing, like unexpectedly high shipping fees for certain postcodes or rising transaction costs from a payment processor. This gives you the clarity to make smarter decisions about pricing, promotions, and which products to feature, ensuring every sale actually contributes to your company’s growth. Measuring the Real ROI of Your AI Investment Investing in new tech always boils down to one question for founders, CMOs, and finance leads: what’s the actual return? When it comes to AI for business intelligence , you have to move past the buzzwords and get to tangible financial outcomes. The good news is, the return on investment here isn’t theoretical. It shows up in real, measurable improvements across your entire operation. An AI-powered BI system isn’t another line item on your P&L; it’s a revenue and efficiency engine. By serving up proactive insights, it directly impacts the KPIs that matter most to an e-commerce brand. This means you can build a business case that’s clear, compelling, and backed by hard numbers. Identifying Hard Metrics for ROI Calculation The most direct way to measure the value of AI is by tracking the “hard” metrics—the numbers that hit your bottom line. These are the KPIs where a dedicated AI analyst can make an immediate and significant difference. You can expect to see clear wins in a few key areas: Increased Customer Lifetime Value (CLV) : AI spots at-risk customers before they churn and pinpoints your most valuable segments. This lets you tailor retention efforts and personalised offers that keep them buying for longer. Reduced Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) : By automatically flagging underperforming ad campaigns and suggesting where to reallocate spend, AI optimises your marketing budget in real time. Every pound you spend works harder to bring in the right customers. Higher Conversion Rates : AI can connect the dots between marketing activities and on-site behaviour to identify friction points in the customer journey, helping you make data-driven changes that actually lift conversions. Lower Operational Costs : Predictive inventory management helps prevent costly stockouts on your bestsellers while avoiding overstocking slow-moving items. That frees up working capital and warehouse space. Calculating the ROI becomes a simple exercise of tracking the “before and after” for these metrics. For a deeper dive into this, you might find our guide on how to measure marketing ROI effectively useful. The Value of Soft Benefits While hard numbers are crucial, the “soft” benefits of AI-driven intelligence often deliver just as much long-term value. These advantages are all about improving the speed and quality of your team’s decision-making, which creates a massive competitive edge. The greatest soft benefit is replacing uncertainty with confidence. When your team trusts the data, they can make bold, strategic decisions faster, seizing opportunities while competitors are still digging through spreadsheets. This shift creates a more agile and data-literate culture. Instead of spending hours debating opinions in meetings, your teams can get instant, data-backed answers to their most pressing questions. This increased operational velocity means you can react to market changes, launch campaigns, and solve problems far more quickly than before. A Framework for Your Business Case The impact of AI on business is undeniable. The UK’s AI sector exploded in 2023, with total revenues surging 34% to add £3.6 billion to the economy. For e-commerce, this boom means more machine learning-driven tools are available, with the share of firms offering ML products jumping from 21% to 35% . And with 92% of AI adopters seeing revenue gains, the ROI is becoming incredibly clear. You can discover more about these AI sector findings on the government’s official site. To build your own business case, combine both hard and soft metrics. Start by calculating the financial upside from a modest improvement—say, a 5% reduction in CAC or a 10% increase in CLV for a key segment. Then, factor in the time your team saves by automating manual reporting and analysis. When you add it all up, the financial justification for investing in AI-driven intelligence becomes crystal clear. Your Roadmap to Implementing AI-Powered BI Getting started with AI for business intelligence doesn’t mean hiring a team of data scientists or kicking off a massive, multi-year project. The latest generation of tools has made implementation a straightforward process designed for business leaders, not just technicians. Let’s walk through a practical roadmap that demystifies the steps and keeps the focus squarely on business outcomes. The journey doesn’t start with technology. It starts with a simple question: What are the most important business problems you need to solve? Answering that gives you the focus you need to guide the entire process and ensures you start getting valuable insights from day one. Connecting Your Key Data Sources First things first, you need to bring all your information together. An effective AI analyst needs the full picture of your business, which means seamlessly connecting the data from the platforms you already rely on every single day. This usually involves connecting key sources like: E-commerce Platform: Your Shopify store is the source of truth for all things sales, products, and customers. Advertising Platforms: Pulling in data from Meta, Google Ads, and TikTok Ads lets the AI connect your ad spend directly to sales outcomes. Email and SMS: Platforms like Klaviyo show how your retention marketing is actually influencing customer lifetime value. Modern AI tools make this incredibly simple. It’s often just a few clicks to authorise access—no custom coding required. Defining Proactive Alerts and Metrics Once your data is flowing, the next step is to tell your AI analyst what to watch for. title: What is a sous chef?
summary: What is a sous chef? We're here to lay it out for you. Read on for details on what sous chefs do, what they earn, & how to become one.
body_text: If you’re curious about culinary careers, you might wonder: what is a sous chef? Simply put, a sous chef runs the day-to-day operations of a kitchen, turning the executive chef’s vision into reality. While executive chefs set the direction, the sous chef leads the team that makes it all happen. Sous chefs at a glance A sous chef is the second-in-command in the kitchen. If the executive chef is the CEO, the sous chef is like the vice president — the right hand who ensures everything runs smoothly. They take a hands-on role in managing the team, coordinating daily operations, and keeping the kitchen on track. Sous chefs oversee all aspects of the kitchen, from inventory to cooking techniques, often specializing in a particular cuisine or style. Beyond culinary skills, a great sous chef is a strong leader. They guide the staff, communicate expectations clearly, and handle mistakes with both skill and understanding. Flexibility, organization, and the ability to problem-solve are all essential traits for keeping the kitchen running like clockwork. What is a sous chef responsible for? There’s no typical day in the life of a sous chef. One shift might be spent planning daily specials and ordering supplies, while the next could have them working hands-on at the sauté or grill station. Their responsibilities span both the creative and operational sides of the kitchen. Managing Costs and Supplies Sous chefs are responsible for keeping kitchen costs under control, balancing quality ingredients with budget constraints. They track inventory, order from vendors, and ensure the kitchen is fully stocked for each service. Overseeing Kitchen Operations From coordinating schedules to maintaining sanitation and safety standards, sous chefs ensure the kitchen runs smoothly. They supervise staff, guide cleaning routines, and step in during emergencies, such as covering a missing shift. Staff Leadership and Communication A sous chef is both a manager and a mentor. They keep the team aligned with the kitchen’s goals, communicate clearly under pressure, and provide guidance when problems arise. They also serve as the bridge between the executive chef and the kitchen staff, helping turn the executive chef’s vision into reality while suggesting improvements when needed. Menu Planning and Creative Support Working closely with the executive chef, sous chefs assist in planning menus, blending logistical planning with culinary creativity. Their hands-on experience ensures that new dishes are practical, achievable, and consistent with the restaurant’s standards. The Path to Becoming a Sous Chef If you’re asking, “What is a sous chef?” it helps to understand the hierarchy of a professional kitchen. Like many organizations, kitchens have different levels, with each role handling specific tasks — from basic prep work to high-level management. Sous chefs rank near the top, overseeing several positions beneath them. Dishwasher Dishwashers handle cleaning cutlery, dishes, and cookware. It’s an entry-level role that keeps the kitchen running smoothly. Prep Cook Prep cooks prepare ingredients for cooking, such as chopping vegetables and assisting with basic cleaning. Formal training isn’t always required, but it can improve job prospects. Commis Chef A commis chef is a junior cook who works under a line cook to gain hands-on experience. Many commis chefs are culinary students or recent graduates. Line Cook Line cooks, or station cooks, manage a specific area of the kitchen, like pastry, vegetables, or meat. They may work independently or with a small team in larger kitchens. Sous Chef The sous chef, or second chef, is the right hand of the head or executive chef. They bridge management and hands-on work, stepping in wherever needed. Flexibility, quick thinking, and business management skills are just as important as culinary expertise. Sous chefs are more common in larger kitchens, while smaller kitchens may not have this role. Head Chef The head chef manages daily kitchen operations, including supervising staff, handling vendors, and overseeing menus and budgets. In smaller kitchens, the head chef is the top authority. Executive Chef The executive chef is the highest-ranking leader in a kitchen, usually in large or high-end restaurants. Famous chefs like Gordon Ramsay hold this title. Executive chefs focus on management, planning menus, collaborating with vendors, and overseeing multiple locations, rather than cooking every day. Working Your Way Up to Sous Chef The first step to becoming a sous chef is landing an entry-level position. Instawork offers a variety of shifts for dishwashers and prep cooks with above-average pay , making it a great way to break into the industry. You can also apply directly to local kitchens or seek apprenticeships. Since traditional kitchens operate on a strict hierarchy, starting at the bottom and gaining experience is essential. Attending culinary school can accelerate your path, but a degree isn’t required. Many sous chefs advance through years of hands-on experience. Professional programs can help you stand out, and certifications — like those from the American Culinary Federation (ACF) — can further boost your credentials. ACF certification typically requires five years of experience in entry-level roles, such as commis chef or line cook. Ultimately, the key to becoming a sous chef is gaining as much real-world kitchen experience as possible. What Is a Sous Chef’s Salary? As of 2026, sous chefs in the U.S. typically earn between $50,000 and $65,000 per year, with top earners making over $67,000 . That breaks down to roughly $25–$31 per hour , with an average around $27/hour . Salaries vary depending on experience, location, and type of workplace. For example, sous chefs in California can earn over $61,000 per year, while those in smaller markets like Missouri may earn closer to $53,000 . Platforms like Instawork also offer chef shifts that can pay above the local average , giving aspiring sous chefs opportunities to earn more while gaining valuable hands-on experience. body_text: 达美航空连续13年荣登《财富》“全球最受赞赏公司”榜单 达美航空公司荣登《财富》杂志“全球最受赞赏公司”榜单，名列第11位，这也是达美航空连续第13年获此荣誉。 Staff Writer Jan 26, 2026 12:06am 达美航空公司荣登《财富》杂志“ 全球最受赞赏公司 ”榜单，名列第11位，这也是达美航空连续第13年获此荣誉。 《财富》杂志主编兼首席内容官Alyson Shontell表示：“《财富》杂志荣幸地向本年度入选‘全球最受赞赏公司’榜单的企业致以祝贺。它们为真正的创新、韧性领导力，以及全球影响力树立了标杆。 在人工智能等技术飞速发展、重塑各行各业的当下，这些企业凭借持续进化的能力、清晰的目标与前瞻的视野脱颖而出，持续为全球商业发展以及未来的工作与管理模式指明方向。“ 达美航空凭借安全可靠的服务和体贴周到的企业文化，持续赢得数百万乘客的信赖，这一切都离不开全体达美员工的敬业奉献。 达美航空首席执行官Ed Bastian表示：达美员工始终恪尽己责、追求卓越，为乘客奉上其期待的一流服务，我为他们感到无比自豪。这份荣誉属于我们这支由全球顶尖的航空专业人才组成的团队，正是他们对卓越品质的执着坚守，推动着达美航空不断前进。“ 2025年达美航空迎来百年华诞，与此同时，全体达美员工亦推动多项重大投资落地，通过一系列举措升级并重塑乘客出行体验，具体包括： 应用程序体验升级： 达美航空应用程序在 7.0 及 7.5 版本中新增实时航班动态推送、个性化通知、自助服务功能等多项优化体验。 人工智能创新落地： 应用程序内搭载的人工智能助手“ 达美礼宾服务 ”（Delta Concierge）开启公测，为飞凡里程常客计划（SkyMiles）会员提供实时化、个性化服务支持。达美的 行李智能管理系统 （Baggage AI）整合实时航班数据、行李定位信息及中转时长，为行李配送人员规划最优路线，助力行李转运效率提升近30%，全面优化行李处理整体表现。 机上餐饮服务焕新 ：从与名厨 José Andrés 展开全新合作，携手 顶级香槟品牌泰亭哲 达成独家机上供应，到将 Shake Shack 引入云端并扩大覆盖范围，达美航空正将机上餐饮逐步打造为媲美餐厅的体验。 贵宾室开幕及拓展： 2025 年是达美飞凡贵宾室（Delta Sky Club）快速发展的一年： 西雅图机场 全新揭幕达美至臻商务舱贵宾室及飞凡贵宾室； 亚特兰大机场 与 盐湖城机场 新增两家飞凡贵宾室；奥兰多机场与费城机场的现有贵宾室已完成扩建升级。 可持续发展成果： 2025 年，达美航空在实现脱碳目标上取得 实质性进展 ，包括投资新一代机型、提升运营效率以及扩大可持续航空燃料（SAF）的应用规模。 地面服务体验优化 ：达美航空进一步升级乘客的地面体验： 达美至臻商务舱专属值机区 服务扩展至美国全部枢纽机场；在各枢纽机场推出 美国运输安全管理局（TSA）预检无接触身份核验服务 ；并通过 “一站式安检”等技术升级简化国际中转流程。此外，达美航空 与优步（Uber）合作重塑送机体验 ，在拉瓜迪亚机场与亚特兰大机场推出“达美×优步优先送机”服务。 达美航空凭借行业领先的服务水准屡获认可，近期第五次蝉联Cirium评定的“ 北美最准点航企 ”，入选 《财富》杂志“年度百强雇主”榜单 并位列第15名，同时在 《福布斯》“2025年全球最佳雇主”榜单 中高居第2位。 《财富》杂志“全球最受赞赏公司”榜单的评选流程： 该榜单的评选基于《财富》杂志与光辉国际合作开展的调研。调研从约1500家候选企业开始，最终筛选出来自31个国家和地区、营收领先的685家企业。 为确定最受认可的公司，光辉国际要求企业高管、董事和行业分析师，根据管理质量、产品质量、社会责任、人才吸引等九个维度，对他们所在行业的企业进行评分。而企业的得分必须在其行业调查中排名前50%才有可能上榜。 为选出50强“全明星”榜单企业，光辉国际邀请企业高管、董事和行业证券分析师选出自己最为赞赏的十家公司，并根据多项评选标准为每家公司打分。候选名单的准入条件为：上一年度调研中综合排名前25%的公司；上一年度在所属行业中排名前三的公司（非美国公司为前四）；或上一年度入选榜单前50、但未满足上述任一条件的公司。评委可为任何行业的任何公司投票。 Related Topics: Fortune Most Admired , Awards © 2026 Delta Air Lines, Inc.

title: Introducing Folders for Chat Sessions
summary: Organize your work the way you think about it. Folders and subfolders bring structure to your Doe sessions.
body_text: As teams use Doe for more of their work, the sidebar gets busy. Sessions pile up, and finding that analysis you ran last week means scrolling through everything else you've done since. Today we're shipping folders - a simple way to organize your chat sessions into a structure that makes sense for how you work. How It Works Create folders directly from the sidebar. Drag sessions into them. Nest folders inside other folders if you need deeper organization. That's it. No complexity, no configuration. Just the kind of file organization you'd expect from any tool that holds your work. Automatic File Saving Every chat session that produces an output - whether that's a chart, image, spreadsheet, or any other file - automatically saves those files to a subfolder within your session. No more hunting through downloads or wondering where that visualization went. This means your folders don't just organize conversations, they organize all the artifacts those conversations create. Export a financial model, generate a report, or create a data visualization, and it's all there waiting for you in one place. Ways Teams Are Using It The flexibility means everyone organizes differently, but we've seen some common patterns emerge: By project - A folder for each initiative, with sessions grouped by what they relate to. When a project wraps, collapse the folder and move on. By workflow - Recurring work like weekly reports, monthly reconciliations, or quarterly planning each get their own folder. Easy to find the last time you ran something similar. By client or account - For teams doing work across multiple customers, a folder per account keeps everything separated and easy to hand off. By team member - Managers creating a folder for each direct report, collecting 1:1 prep, feedback drafts, and performance notes in one place. Small Feature, Real Impact Folders won't change what Doe can do. But they change how it feels to use Doe over time. Instead of a growing list of sessions that blurs together, you get a workspace that reflects your actual work. The feature is live now for all users. Open your sidebar and start organizing.

title: Solid Power Announces Pricing of $130 Million Registered Direct Offering
What successful remote workers do differently
summary: Discover what successful remote workers do differently from those who struggle.
body_text: I don’t think I have to quote him verbatim, but Albert Einstein denounced doing the same thing over and over again and expecting a different result. While it might be competitive, remote work presents you with limitless opportunities to land international gigs. In reality, the people who succeed at remote work approach it very differently from those who struggle or burn out. It is not a mere coincidence or sheer luck. Their success strategy goes beyond tools and skills, but is more about habits, mindset, and systems. Here’s what successful remote workers consistently do differently. Also read: How global work culture is changing the way we live and earn They treat remote work as a career While remote work might look simple on the outside, promising flexible hours and the freedom to work from anywhere, it is still a career. Successful remote workers don’t see remote work as a convenient work-life option. They treat it as a real career choice that requires structure, planning, discipline, and sustainable growth. They invest in their skills, track their performance, and strive for improvement. This mindset helps them make better decisions, hone their craft, and negotiate better. They build systems To be honest, it is easy to get comfortable when you are working from home. You might start waiting for motivation to work, or get carried away by distractions. Successful remote workers don’t move this way. They are committed to building sustainable systems and work structures that support productivity. Daily routines, defined work hours, clear task management processes, and communication rules are key to succeeding as a remote worker. They ensure clear communication Strong communication is very relevant when working in the digital workspace. You are collaborating with people from different cultures, across borders, with varying expectations, and in different time zones. Successful remote workers have mastered the art of communication. They clarify expectations early and provide regular updates without being asked. By communicating clearly and consistently, they build trust with managers, clients, and teammates across time zones. They manage their energy Remote work can blur the line between work and life. Paying attention to your energy levels can be key to ensuring productivity. Successful remote workers schedule tough tasks for when they are still fresh and alert. Fill the remaining time with breaks, sleep, and leisure activities. This structure prevents burnout, especially when working across multiple time zones. LDMAG1 They take control of their finances Unlike traditional employees, remote work puts you in charge of your finances, especially if you are earning a foreign income. Many remote workers lack a reliable payment setup and miss out on global opportunities. The secret to successful remote work is learning to manage finances more effectively with multicurrency accounts. With this setup, they streamline their finances, cut down on transaction fees, and convert to local currencies when the rates are favourable. They are intentional about location That remote work gives you the freedom to work from anywhere doesn’t mean you can work from everywhere. It is easy to fantasise about being nomadic and moving around with work. If this isn't well planned, you might end up in a location that doesn’t favour remote work. This is what successful remote workers do differently. They choose locations with robust digital infrastructure, strong internet coverage, budget-friendly living costs, favourable time zones, and budding communities that support productivity. They can go as far as trying out locations on a short-term basis before committing to a long-term one. Also read: What remote workers should plan before relocating They understand the importance of networking Working remotely does not mean working in isolation. A lot goes on behind the scenes, and only those who are privy to such information can plug in. Successful remote workers actively build relationships online and offline. They participate in professional communities, attend virtual or in-person events, use their platforms to promote their work, and strive for visibility within their spaces. These lead to referrals, collaborations, and more opportunities that are difficult to access through job boards alone. Managing your finances like a smart remote worker Whether you think your remote work journey isn’t looking great or you haven’t even started, it is usually a good idea to learn from successful remote workers. The difference between struggling remote workers and successful ones is not often about talent. Successful remote workers are intentional about every aspect of their work, including how they manage their finances. Many opt for Grey because the payment platform offers USD, GBP, and EUR accounts, making international transactions easy to manage. With Grey, you get more than low fees and competitive exchange rates , but also automated invoicing and a virtual USD debit card to manage your international spending. You can link your Grey account with global freelancing platforms to withdraw your earnings swiftly. Sign up on Grey and download the app and join the clique of successful remote workers who manage their earnings efficiently. ‍

title: Comparing Fraud Taxonomies and How to Use Them
summary: The fraud industry is finally getting the taxonomy frameworks it needs. From the Fed's classification standards to Stripe's MITRE-inspired FT3 framework, new models are helping teams organize fraud data, automate detection, and coordinate across cyber, fraud, and AML functions.
body_text: By Arjun Bisen, CEO & Co-Founder | January 29, 2026 ‍ I’ve been in many conversations with cyber, intel, and fraud experts where they’ve praised taxonomies like the MITRE ATT@CK framework and sharing of Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) that are commonly understood in cyber intelligence and wished that the fraud taxonomy was as well developed. That would allow them to throw all the fraud accounts/ IOCs into a centralized system to take automated action/ scoring. That said, there are some very useful fraud taxonomies that are being worked on by some of the best in the business, which could have a big impact on how we organize. Each of the major frameworks focus on solving a different problem. The Fed’s FraudClassifier has become a foundational standard for banks and payment providers. Its strength is simplicity: a clear, payment-agnostic way to distinguish authorized vs. unauthorized fraud and report losses consistently across the industry. The Fed’s ScamClassifier builds on this by addressing a major blind spot, authorized scams. By breaking scams into concrete types (romance, investment, impersonation, etc.), it added much-needed clarity to an area that was previously vague, on the rise, and inconsistently labeled. The Fed has a useful guide on how to leverage this classifier. The most tactical of all, the FT3 framework, built by Vincent Passaro and the good people at Stripe , takes a very different approach. Modeled after cybersecurity frameworks like MITRE ATT&CK, it classifies fraud by the tactics and techniques used by attackers. This is powerful for detection and threat intelligence, but also more complex to operationalize. However, as a technology company, we’ve found useful ways to leverage their Github repo to automate the classification fraud materials, leveraging our AI agents. We’re always happy to share our approach with anyone interested. Finally, FS-ISAC ’s Cyber Fraud Prevention Framework focuses less on classification and more on coordination. By mapping fraud across stages, from reconnaissance to monetization, it helps break down silos between fraud, cyber, and AML teams. It's especially useful and organizing info sharing via FS-ISAC's platform. The takeaway: there’s no single “best” taxonomy. The strongest fraud programs combine: • Fed models for standardization and reporting • FT3 for understanding adversary behavior • FS-ISAC’s framework for cross-team action How are you all using these taxonomies today? What did I miss? I generally feel like the data we need to tackle fraud exists but often sits in silos, is unstructured, and could really benefit from tighter classification that would allow it to be operationalized in a simple way.

title: Ohio Medicaid Income Limits (2026): the numbers, the common sticking points, and what to do next
summary: Figuring out Ohio Medicaid income limits shouldn't feel like a second job—but for many families trying to access in-home care, it does. Whether you're exploring PASSPORT, MyCare Ohio, or Structured Family Caregiving, income is often the first hurdle you'll face. This guide breaks down the 2026 income limits by category, explains when assets matter (and when they don't), and walks you through what to do if you're over the limit. Includes current income charts, eligibility pathways for long-term care support, and practical next steps for Ohio families navigating Medicaid.
body_text: If you’re trying to get help for yourself or a loved one through Ohio Medicaid, you’ve probably noticed something quickly: the care decisions are hard enough, and the financial rules can feel like a second job. You’re not alone in that. Income limits are often the first “gate” families run into—especially when the goal isn’t just health coverage, but in-home support through programs like PASSPORT, MyCare Ohio, or Structured Family Caregiving. This guide keeps it simple: which category you’re in, what the 2025 income limits look like, when assets matter, and where to go next. Figure out which Medicaid category applies Ohio Medicaid has different eligibility categories, and each category has its own income rules. The easiest way to start is to place yourself (or your loved one) into one of these groups: Parents and Caretakers: generally family members raising children such as grandchildren, nieces/nephews, etc. Adults ages 19–64 (no Medicare): often called Expansion Medicaid Children and pregnant people: often through Ohio’s Healthy Start coverage Seniors (65+) and people with disabilities: often called ABD Medicaid (Aged, Blind, or Disabled) People applying for long-term care or Medicaid waivers: similar to ABD, but with long-term care financial rules and a required “level of care” assessment If you’re exploring home-based support, it can also help to read our overview of waiver options here: Ohio Medicaid Waiver Guide 2025 income limits in Ohio (quick chart) Many Ohio Medicaid categories use percentages of the Federal Poverty Level (FPL) to determine their financial eligibility according to their gross income. Below are monthly income amounts for some of the most common Modified Adjusted Gross Income (MAGI) groups. source Note: Some 2026 figures have not yet been published by the state as of the writing of this blog. Where 2026 numbers are unavailable, 2025 figures are used and will be updated as new data becomes available. A few helpful reminders: Household size matters (and it isn’t always as simple as “who lives in the home”). Taxes and dependents can change how Medicaid counts a household. These figures are about income. Whether savings matter depends on the category (see the asset section below). If you’re slightly above the limit, it may still be worth applying—some applicants qualify due to how income is calculated. If you’re applying for PASSPORT, MyCare Ohio, or other long-term care support If your goal is in-home long-term care services (or support that helps someone stay out of a nursing facility), you’re usually dealing with the long-term care/waiver side of Medicaid eligibility. In many long-term care pathways, Ohio uses a separate “special income” cap. A commonly used figure for 2026 is: $2,982 per month This part matters if you’re trying to access programs such as: PASSPORT (older adults): Exploring the PASSPORT Waiver Structured Family Caregiving (paid live-in caregiving in certain waiver arrangements): Structured Family Caregiving guide A broader step-by-step application walk-through: How to Apply for Caregiving Benefits in Ohio Asset limits: when savings count (and when they don’t) This is one of the biggest points of confusion, and it’s also where people sometimes assume they’re disqualified when they aren’t. Expansion Medicaid / children / pregnancy coverage: typically no asset test (meaning savings and resources are usually not part of eligibility). ABD Medicaid and long-term care/waiver pathways: typically do have an asset/resource limit (often around $2,000 for an individual, with different rules for couples). Assets can include things like cash, checking/savings accounts, and some investments. Certain items—like a primary residence and car—may be treated differently depending on the situation. If assets are a concern in your case, it’s worth getting help early so you don’t rely on assumptions. If you’re over the limit, you may still have options Seeing a number that’s higher than the chart can feel discouraging. But “over the limit” doesn’t always mean there’s no path forward. MAGI categories (Expansion, many children/pregnancy cases): a 5% income disregard can help some applicants who are near the cutoff. Medicaid Spend-Down: If your income is above the limit but you have regular medical expenses, you may be able to "spend down" the excess each month by applying medical costs toward your eligibility—once your medical bills equal or exceed the amount you're over the limit, you can qualify for Medicaid for the rest of that month. Because these situations are fact-specific, many families choose to apply anyway and follow up with the agency handling the case, rather than ruling themselves out upfront. How to apply for Medicaid in Ohio You can apply in any of these ways: Online: Ohio Benefits portal (benefits.ohio.gov) Phone: Ohio Medicaid Consumer Hotline: 1-800-324-8680 In person: your County Job and Family Services (JFS) office A few documents that often help: ID and proof of Ohio residency Proof of income (pay stubs, Social Security award letter, pension statements, etc.) Medicare card (if applicable) Basic household information If your goal is paid caregiving or in-home waiver services after Medicaid approval, this guide lays out the next steps: How to Apply for Caregiving Benefits in Ohio (PASSPORT, MyCare Ohio, and Structured Family Caregiving) Choose the path that fits your situation If you’re looking for support at home, the most helpful next step is usually to match the right program to your situation: Seniors who want to remain at home: PASSPORT Waiver guide Live-in family caregiving arrangements: Structured Family Caregiving guide A practical step-by-step application guide: How to Apply for Caregiving Benefits in Ohio On a MyCare plan already? Here's what's changing in 2026: NextGen MyCare – What you need to know for 2026 If you want help understanding which program fits your goals (and what the application process looks like), you can also contact CareOasis to talk through next steps.

title: Whatnot's 2026 State of Live Selling Report: Time to Go Live
summary: We’re excited to share our 2026 State of Live Selling Report with you, the most comprehensive report on live selling to date. It combines Whatnot platform data with survey insights from thousands of live sellers across the U.S., U.K., France, and Germany to show how the industry is evolving, the inc
body_text: We’re excited to share our 2026 State of Live Selling Report with you, the most comprehensive report on live selling to date. It combines Whatnot platform data with survey insights from thousands of live sellers across the U.S., U.K., France, and Germany to show how the industry is evolving, the incredible success businesses are having because of going live, the categories that are going to be big this year, and how the industry is having a real, positive impact on local economies. The report shows what our community already knows: live commerce is outperforming. In our survey of live sellers across platforms, nearly nine in ten say live selling drives stronger sales than traditional e-commerce. More than half now generate the majority of their revenue through live selling. For many, it’s solving their biggest business challenges: reaching new customers, increasing repeat buyers, and converting at higher rates. Eighty-eight percent of sellers believe businesses that don’t adopt live selling will struggle to stay competitive. The live shopping market has reached an estimated $22 billion across North America and Europe, with Whatnot having nearly 60 percent market share. As the category leader, Whatnot is where sellers are building. In 2025, sellers drove $8 billion in live sales, more than doubling the year before. The seller base is scaling just as quickly: one in eight Whatnot sellers is now full time, up 20 percent year over year. Sellers who go live 3-4 times per week average over $13,000 in monthly sales and over 20 million new accounts were created last year, expanding the buyer base for every business on Whatnot. Europe is growing just as fast. The seller base grew 600 percent year over year. France is adding new sellers faster than any market, up 888 percent. In the U.K., sellers who go live every day are averaging £30K a month. In Germany, sellers are making €475 per hour they're live, more than anywhere else. “When I look at the rise of live selling today, I don’t see a trend.
